recaps.title: Sample: 2025 Week 1 Recap
recaps.dateLabel: Sample format — last season’s Week 1 finals (not 2026)
recaps.coldOpen: Welcome to IDP country, where 220 is a Tuesday and 250 is a personality. Week 1 reminded everyone: offense sells tickets, defense runs up the scoreboard. Hero of the week: anybody with a green jersey and a tackle. Goat of the week: whoever brought a Fantrax projection to a gunfight.
heroes: Myles Garrett (TTAB) — 42 on DL, ruined someone’s Sunday
S. Dennis (Eddies) — 35 IDP, the quiet assassin
goats: Saltese’s Week 1 script — 184.5 while Bill hit 244
The Big Unit — 173 in a league that averages 220+
Anyone who started the week trusting Fantrax IDP math

matchups.scoreline: Towner Top Aga Bottom 254.5, Indian Trail Slumlords 251.5
matchups.blurb: Three. Points. Chase’s barnburner had everything: Josh Allen going nuclear for 50 (394 pass, 2 pass TD, 2 rush TD), Myles Garrett deleting the pocket for 42 (2 sacks, 5 tackles, 4 TFL), and Roquan Smith + Fred Warner stacking 25 and 22 on the second level. Offense 124.5, IDP 130 — defense outscored the skill players and it still almost wasn’t enough. Towner answered with Herbert’s 40, Bijan Robinson’s all-purpose 37, and a DB party (Witherspoon 22, Woods pick). Slumlords put up 251.5 and lost. In most leagues that’s a statement win. Here it’s a polite funeral. Juice: Allen, Garrett, Roquan. Junk: leaving a 254.5 on the table by three.

Kyle wins ugly again — dual-era champ tax. Puka dropped 29, Daniels chipped 22, and the IDP (Hamilton 27, Q. Williams 24) did just enough. Tim’s side was an IDP manifesto: Okereke 32 on 16 tackles, Henley 24, Van Ginkel 22, Cross 23, Holland 17 — Divers defense alone put up 153. Offense? A polite 67.5. You can win this league with a magazine-cover defense and a backup-looking offense… unless Doubtpfizer remembers how to close. Margin: 2.5. Heart rate: illegal in some states. Juice: Okereke’s tackle farm, Puka. Junk: Morningside’s skill-player quiet hours.

Bill brought the IDP house party and left Luke holding the mop. Eddies defense: 145 — S. Dennis 35, Jordyn Brooks 31, Deablo 21, Winters 22 — while Kyler/McBride/Egbuka kept the offense respectable at 99. Saltese managed 80.5 on offense (Nix’s 6-point dud will live in Slack forever) and 104 on IDP. Garrett Wilson and Sutton tried; Baun’s 24 wasn’t enough cover. Commish gets the early memo: the gavel doesn’t score tackles. Juice: Dennis, Brooks, Bill’s second level. Junk: Nix’s Week 1 tape, 184.5 in a 220 league.

Ceiling check for the format. Hot Coffee’s IDP put up 161 by itself — Khalil Mack 31, Fred Warner 26, Jordan Hicks 24, T.J. Watt 23 — every defensive starter cleared 18. That’s not a unit, that’s a tax audit. Offense was ‘merely’ 94.5 (Kupp 24.5, Mahomes/Hall 18). Puka Shells hit 219.5 with Allen’s 28 and a sturdy 134 IDP (Bentley/White) and still looked like the away team at a funeral. 219 wins most leagues on Earth. In Wheels Up it’s a handshake and a ‘tough one.’ Juice: Mack-Warner-Watt starter pack. Junk: thinking 219 was safe.

matchups.scoreline: The Longest Yard 218.5, The Big Unit 173
matchups.blurb: Alumni energy, modern scoring. Longest Yard cleared the bar with Evans 23 and an IDP floor that held (E. Jones 24, Granderson 20) for 218.5. The Big Unit brought Tyreek’s 26 and… not much else on defense (80 IDP). 173 in a league that lives at 220+ is how you become a cautionary waiver tale by Week 2. If your IDP week looks like The Big Unit, start texting the FAAB group chat. Juice: Evans + enough tackles. Junk: 80 IDP points. That’s a lifestyle choice.

recaps.closer: Template for Tuesdays: cold open → every scoreline with smack → heroes/goats. First live 2026 drop lands after Week 1 finals (Tue 9/15). WWJDD.
